items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So then I met Art Tatum and we became friends. He used to live right across the street from me.

ctx.x: So as I was just about to go out the door I heard this crescendo on the piano. They brought this kid up on the bandstand, led him up on the bandstand and I heard this great crescendo on the piano and I turned around and went back. And it was Art Tatum. And he started out playing Tiger Rag, right

off the bat. And this I had to acknowledge, you know. So then I met Art Tatum and we became friends. He used to live right across the street from me. I lived right across the street from him, rather, in Toledo in City Park.

And he had a grand collection of Earl Hines records. That was his favorite piano player at that time. And so then I stayed around Toledo with this band all that summer and I played with Art and I played with Teddy Wilson at the Chateau of France because we had a little group. It was Art Tatum that we used to run around. We were all teenagers and we had a little group like -- of course, that was 1931, I was 21 years old at that time. And we ran together after we got off from our respective jobs.
